newsitem.title: UK: Siebe makes recommended APV offer.
newsitem.headline: Siebe makes recommended APV offer.

text.p: British engineering group Siebe Plc and engineering and components group APV Plc on Friday announced a recommended offer for APV shares not owned by Siebe. The offer values APV at approximately 327.4 million pounds ($531.7 million) and each APV share at 105 pence.

"The offer is 0.10955 new Siebe shares for each APV share with a full cash alternative of 97.5 pence per APV share provided by Siebe and Morgan Stanley," the companies said in a joint statement. Siebe already owns almost three percent of APV shares.

The firms said the Siebe offer meant APV shareholders would benefit from a premium of 72 percent to the company's share price on April 21, the day before Siebe's approach. The APV board said it unanimously recommended shareholders to accept the offer.

"Following several years of restructuring designed to concentrate APV's business and improve operational efficiency, we believe APV is better positioned for 1997 and beyond," Mike Smith, APV's chairman, said.

Barrie Stephens, Siebe's chairman, said the integration of APV into Siebe would unlock significant growth potential for APV, giving it access to "world class" process automation systems and technology. "There are...significant growth opportunities, clear operating synergies and the combination of the two companies will create increased shareholder value," he added.
The firms said significant cost benefits were expected to be achieved by combining Siebe's and APV's global networks of local engineering, contracting and customer service organisations.
